bug_semantics: LiquidJS pop (src/filters/array.ts) clones its input with [...toArray(v)] and returns clone.pop() without charging this.context.memoryLimit.use(...). After memoryLimit existed, sibling array-clone filters (shift, unshift, compact, concat, reverse, slice, map, uniq, and others) deducted array.length before allocating, so {{ huge | shift }} with a tight memoryLimit threw 'memory alloc limit exceeded' while {{ huge | pop }} completed an O(N) clone bounded only by the Node heap (CWE-770). The pop signature also omitted this: FilterImpl, so it had no typed access to the limiter. Exploitability requires memoryLimit to be set and a template that pops an attacker-sized array.
flaw_origin: The unguarded pop clone was first written in 258780e9a87ce87534a6bb4336725cb1d38a2998 (feat: pop/shift/unshift filters from Jekyll, v10.11.0). That commit added pop, shift, and unshift as identical uncharged [...toArray(v)] clones; memoryLimit did not exist yet. git log -L :pop:src/filters/array.ts then shows no further rewrite of those pop lines until the fix. The security asymmetry named by the advisory was created later by e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 (feat: DoS prevention, #250, v10.15.0), which introduced Limiter/memoryLimit and charged shift/unshift and the other array-clone filters while leaving pop's original body unchanged. The BIC is the first-write of the vulnerable pop lines, not the later incomplete sibling hardening.

reasoning: CVE-2026-55575 / GHSA-g357-x5c3-c72p is a published CWE-770 memoryLimit bypass in LiquidJS pop, not a withdrawn or rejected advisory. The sink is the pop filter's full-array clone without a memoryLimit.use charge, which after v10.15.0 lets {{ arr | pop }} allocate outside the budget that shift/unshift and other array-clone filters enforce. Following git log -L/:S and blame as leads, the smallest public commit that first wrote those pop lines is 258780e9a87ce87534a6bb4336725cb1d38a2998 (Jekyll-parity pop/shift/unshift). Its immediate parent 18d55929e51749def0239a9163c7d3abc0d2cf40 has no pop function and no memoryLimit, so this is a first-write rather than a move, refactor, revert, or squash. The same commit also wrote unguarded shift/unshift clones; e443068 later charged those siblings when introducing DoS limits and skipped pop, which is why the GHSA reads as an accidental omission, but e443068 did not author the pop clone and is therefore not the BIC.
